definitions.explanation: With an affirmative predicate, marks a feeling the speaker cannot quite put into words. Very common in なんとも{言|い}えない (indescribable) and before an adjective of impression.

definitions.gloss: not at all; nothing much; no problem
definitions.explanation: With a negative predicate, denies the whole of something — that anything is wrong, that anything can be said, or that anything is felt.

examples.japanese: なんとも{言|い}えない{味|あじ}だ。
なんとも{不思議|ふしぎ}な{話|はなし}ですね。
examples.english: What a strange story that is.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{故郷|こきょう}の{景色|けしき}を{見|み}て、なんとも{懐|なつ}かしい{気持|きも}ちになった。
examples.english: Seeing my hometown scenery after so long filled me with an indescribable nostalgia.

examples.japanese: この{程度|ていど}の{寒|さむ}さならなんとも{思|おも}わない。
examples.english: Cold like this doesn't bother me in the least.

examples.japanese: {結果|けっか}が{出|で}るまでは、なんとも{申|もう}し{上|あ}げられません。
examples.english: Until the results are in, I cannot say anything at all.

notes:
From {何|なん} + と + も. Which sense applies is decided entirely by whether the predicate is affirmative or negative, so read to the end of the clause before interpreting it.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- なんとも{言|い}えない: indescribable; impossible to say either way
- なんとも{思|おも}わない: to think nothing of it, to be unbothered
- なんともない: to be fine, to be nothing serious
- なんとも{申|もう}し{上|あ}げられない: I am not in a position to comment (formal)

USAGE:
Sense 1 before an adjective is a warm, slightly literary intensifier: なんとも{美|うつく}しい (ever so beautiful). Sense 2's なんともない is the standard reply to "are you hurt?" or "is anything wrong?".
